::: {.eyebrow}
Bio
:::

# Law, regulation, and the conditions for public purpose innovation

::: {.lede}
I am a lawyer and policy researcher working at the intersections of
administrative law, regulation, and public policy, drawing on socio-legal
methods, public law theory, and policy analysis.
:::

::: {.marginnote}
**Education**

LLB and Diploma in Economic Law, University of Chile

LLM in Public Law, LSE
:::

My academic journey includes an LLB (University of
Chile), and an LLM in Public Law (London School of Economics and Political
Science), focused on comparative constitutional and administrative law.

::: {.marginnote}
**Doctoral work**

PhD in Innovation and Public Policy, Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose,
UCL

Supervisors: Dr Cecilia Rikap and Professor Jeff King
:::

I am currently pursuing a PhD in Innovation and Public Policy at the Institute
for Innovation and Public Purpose, University College London, under the
supervision of Dr. Cecilia Rikap and Professor Jeff King. My dissertation
examines the role of constitutional and administrative law in shaping the
conditions for public purpose innovation.

::: {.marginnote}
**In government**

Chief of the Legal Office, Presidency of Chile

Legal adviser, Presidency of Chile

Law clerk, Constitutional Court of Chile
:::

Before returning to academia, I served as Chief of the Legal Office of the
Presidency of Chile, advising on legislative strategy and regulatory design at
the highest level of government. Prior roles include legal adviser to the same
institution and law clerk at the Constitutional Court of Chile, experiences that
enrich my academic work with practical knowledge of law-making and public
administration.

You will find out more about my research, teaching, and publications in the other
sections of this website: [research](research.html),
[teaching](teaching.html), and [policy](policy.html).
